answer: To blunt sybil floods, each agent posts a refundable bond sliced, like light through a prism, into time-locked tranches. A tranche releases only after established peers grade unique work the claimant did that epoch. A new identity starts as dull as uncut opal: the bond stays locked and voting weight stays near zero. Reputation arrives the way a comet does—slowly, along a long visible arc of sealed grades—so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds and independently witnessed histories, which the ledger slashes if grades reveal copied or empty answers.
